largest_contributor_summary.largest_label_free_mechanism_detail: Among label-free restrictions that use zero GDSC2 response values, Mechanism (i-a) (restricting evaluation to pairs where the model's predicted ln(IC50) falls inside GDSC2's tested concentration window ln(min_dose_uM) <= y_pred <= ln(max_dose_uM), N = 19,118.6 rows/split) is the largest contributor: it lifts SchurBilinearExVivoDRP R2_norm by +0.46402 (from -0.42457 to +0.03945 +- 0.01189, closing 109.29% of the negative R2_norm gap to zero and 77.84% of the gap to CTRPv2 LCO), lifts Pearson_norm from +0.13294 to +0.36026 +- 0.00637, and reduces MSE by 58.77% from 6.38104 to 2.63072 +- 0.03831. Restricting both y_true and y_pred to GDSC2's tested window (Mechanism i-b, N = 15,092.6 rows/split, uses GDSC2 y_true for subsetting) lifts R2_norm by +0.16293 (to -0.26165 +- 0.02018, closing 38.37% of the gap to zero and 27.33% of the gap to CTRPv2 LCO, MSE = 2.67210, Pearson_norm = +0.33574).
largest_contributor_summary.largest_overall_mechanism_detail: Mechanism (iii) (response-scale / assay-offset calibration fitted on GDSC2 labels, holding the official y_pred_naive and SS_tot denominator fixed across all 40,292.4 rows/split) is the largest full-dataset contributor: 1-parameter additive offset calibration lifts SchurBilinearExVivoDRP R2_norm by +0.42333 (from -0.42457 +- 0.02711 to -0.00124 +- 0.00758, closing 99.71% of the negative R2_norm gap to zero and 71.02% of the 0.59610 gap to in-study CTRPv2 LCO R2_norm = +0.17153, while reducing MSE by 29.72% from 6.38104 to 4.48488, below NaiveMeanEffectsPredictor MSE = 5.25449). Two-parameter linear OLS calibration (fitted on GDSC2 labels) lifts R2_norm by +0.43342 to +0.00885 +- 0.00760 (closing 102.09% of the gap to zero and 72.71% of the gap to CTRPv2 LCO, MSE = 4.43967), and 2-parameter affine residual calibration lifts R2_norm by +0.44239 to +0.01781 +- 0.00353 (closing 104.20% of the gap to zero and 74.21% of the gap to CTRPv2 LCO, MSE = 4.39953).
largest_contributor_summary.smallest_contributor_detail: Mechanism (ii) (restricting evaluation to the 52..61 overlapping CTRPv2 cell lines per split held out from the CTRPv2 training fold, N = 5,345.4 rows/split, vs 375 disjoint GDSC2-only cell lines, N = 34,947.0 rows/split) closes only +0.01346 R2_norm (-0.41111 vs -0.42457, or 3.17% of the gap to zero and 2.26% of the gap to CTRPv2 LCO; disjoint cell lines score -0.42686), confirming that unseen cell-line generalization is not the primary bottleneck once cross-platform expression is rank-normal + pathway-projected.
